# CircleCI CLI

> Command-line interface to CircleCI for use in your terminal or scripts. This is the short index: install, authenticate, install the agent skills, and links to the full reference.

# Getting started
`circleci` is a command-line interface to CircleCI for use in your terminal or your scripts.

## Installation

Pick the entry for your platform. Package managers that need their repository
registered first list the setup command and the install command, in that order.

macOS or Linux — Homebrew:
```shell
brew install circleci
```

Windows — WinGet:
```shell
winget install --id CircleCI.CLI
```

Linux — apt (Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, Raspberry Pi):
```shell
curl -1sLf 'https://packages.circleci.com/public/setup.deb.sh' | sudo -E bash
sudo apt install circleci
```

Linux — rpm (Fedora, RHEL, SUSE, Amazon):
```shell
curl -1sLf 'https://packages.circleci.com/public/setup.rpm.sh' | sudo -E bash
sudo dnf install circleci
```

Linux — Snap:
```shell
sudo snap install circleci
sudo snap connect circleci:password-manager-service
```

Prebuilt binaries and Linux packages for every release are on the
[releases page](https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/releases), and the
[README](https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli#readme) covers the
less common cases.

## Configuration

Run `circleci auth login` to authenticate with your CircleCI account. You can also set the
`CIRCLE_TOKEN` environment variable.

## Get Running

Run `circleci run get` to view the runs for the current project in an interactive terminal UI (TUI).

## AI agents

Using an AI coding agent? Run `circleci help agents` to install CircleCI's skills.

## Model Context Protocol

The CLI supports the MCP protocol. To enable it, run:

Claude:
```shell
circleci mcp claude enable # Enable in Claude desktop
claude mcp add-from-claude-desktop -s user # Add with current user scope
```

Cursor:
```shell
circleci mcp cursor enable
```

VS Code:
```shell
circleci mcp vscode enable
```

## Support

Report bugs or search for existing feature requests in our
[issue tracker](https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/issues)

# Agents
CircleCI publishes skills that teach AI coding agents to use `circleci`: validate config,
watch the run a push started, read failing logs and tests, rerun jobs and debug failed builds.
Further skills cover config tuning, onboarding, deploys and Smarter Testing. The source is at
<https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/skills>.

## Claude Code

```shell
claude plugin marketplace add CircleCI-Public/skills
claude plugin install circleci@circleci-public-skills
```

Or inside a session:

```text
/plugin marketplace add CircleCI-Public/skills
/plugin install circleci@circleci-public-skills
```

## Codex

```shell
codex plugin marketplace add CircleCI-Public/skills
codex plugin add circleci@circleci-skills
```

## Cursor and other agents

The [skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) installer (Node 22.20 or later) supports
Cursor and most other agents; `-a` names the agent. To install the CLI skill:

```shell
npx skills add CircleCI-Public/skills -a cursor --skill circleci-cli
```

`--skill` takes several names, and `--list` shows them all. Leaving `--skill` out installs
every skill in the repository, the Chunk skills included, when an agent runs the command or
`-y` is passed; in a terminal you pick from a list instead.

Pass `-g` to install for your user rather than the current project. Without it, an agent
gets the project, and a terminal asks which you want.

Without Node, copy a skill's folder from `plugins/circleci/skills/` in the repository to
`~/.cursor/skills/<name>`, where `<name>` is the `name` in its `SKILL.md`, so
`skills/cli` becomes `circleci-cli`.

## MCP

`circleci` also runs as an MCP server. Run `circleci mcp claude enable` (Claude Desktop),
`circleci mcp cursor enable` or `circleci mcp vscode enable`. `circleci help getting-started`
shows the extra step for Claude Code.

## Docs for models

- <https://cli.circleci.com/llms.txt>: install, authenticate, and links to the rest
- <https://cli.circleci.com/llms-full.txt>: every command, flag and JSON field

## Reference

- [Full command reference](https://cli.circleci.com/llms-full.txt): every command, flag and JSON field, generated from the live command tree. Large — fetch it when you need command detail.
- [Command reference on the web](https://cli.circleci.com/reference/): the same content as a browsable page.
- [Environment variables](https://cli.circleci.com/reference/#environment): authentication, colour, paging and telemetry. Also `circleci help environment`.
- [Output formatting](https://cli.circleci.com/reference/#formatting): `--json`, `--jq` and templates. Also `circleci help formatting`.
- [Source, issue tracker and prebuilt binaries](https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli)
